model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a clear money edge over Republican Ricardo Cabrera, who reports no fundraising. overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Ricardo Cabrera in a San Diego-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. Jacobs has raised roughly $1.6 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Cabrera reports no fundraising and no outside groups are spending against her. Prediction markets put her chances near 96 percent.

With no public polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the money gap. All of these point the same way, making Jacobs a heavy favorite, though the lack of direct polling keeps the uncertainty band relatively wide for a race of this type.
